item.title: Chemists harness light to build 3D molecular structures for drug discovery
item.description: Researchers from the Department of Chemistry at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), led by Professor Jian He and collaborators, have developed a new light-driven method for constructing three-dimensional molecular building blocks that could give medicinal chemists greater flexibility in designing new drug candidates. The findings have been published in Nature Chemistry. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In 1903, rabbits were released on Hawaii’s Laysan Island as a food source; within a decade...
item.description: German immigrant Max Schlemmer introduced rabbits to Laysan Island in 1903 for business and entertainment. These rabbits rapidly consumed vegetation, leading to the extinction of three unique landbird species. President Theodore Roosevelt established the Hawaiian Islands Bird Reservation to protect the remaining wildlife. Federal authorities later removed Schlemmer and eradicated the invasive rabbit population by 1923. Conservationists have since worked to restore the habitat and reintroduce species to the island. item.title: Genetic evidence reveals how goosegrass colonized a newly formed volcanic island
item.description: Opportunities to directly observe how life colonizes newly formed land and how ecosystems subsequently develop are exceedingly rare. item.title: In 1867, New Zealand introduced brown trout for sport fishing; more than 60 million were released
item.description: In 1867, British settlers introduced brown trout to New Zealand, intending to enhance sport fishing. This decision led to the release of over sixty million trout, which had devastating effects on local fish populations, resulting in declines and even extinction of some native species. The presence of these invasive fish fundamentally changed stream ecosystems and insect behaviors, making their management a significant conservation challenge even today. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Imran Bayoumi, Deputy Director & Resident Fellow at the Atlantic Council.
